records.name: SAFE (post-money valuation cap)
records.one_line: Cash now for shares later, priced by a future round, capped.

mechanics.dilution_range: 5 – 25% at conversion, compounding across multiple SAFEs

disqualifiers.description: prior instrument with anti-dilution that makes conversion unmodellable

provider.motivation: Optionality. Cheap exposure to asymmetric upside with no governance burden and no pricing argument today.
provider.volume: High. Filtered almost entirely on founder and warm-edge provenance.

unlocks: runway to reach a priced round
poisons: priced-seed-preferred if stacked repeatedly at rising caps
triggers: cap table complexity at next round

forecloses: pricing the round on your own terms later — the cap is a ceiling you set before you had leverage

variants.delta: Standard-form, well-understood, post-money is the default since 2018
Used, but convertible notes are the local default; less standard-form consensus, more bespoke drafting
Advance Subscription Agreement is the local analogue and is shaped by investor tax-relief eligibility rather than by simplicity
Widely used, often with local convertible features grafted on

knowledge.failure_modes: SAFE stacking — four SAFEs at four caps and nobody has modelled the conversion; founders discover their real dilution at the priced round. Uncapped SAFEs signed early with an MFN that later ratchets. Conversion never triggering because no priced round ever happens, leaving instruments in permanent limbo.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"A SAFE defers the valuation."* It does not — **the cap is a valuation claim wearing a disguise.** It is your stated ceiling, set at the point of least leverage, and sophisticated investors read it exactly that way. Also: *"it's not dilution yet."* It is; it is dilution with the invoice not yet delivered.
knowledge.ready_signals: A warm angel population; a story that survives 40 seconds; enough product that "what have you built" has an answer.
knowledge.not_ready_signals: No entity. No idea what the cap should be or why. Needing the money to survive rather than to reach a milestone — SAFEs fund progress, not rescue.
knowledge.tells: *"Send me the SAFE and I'll take a look"* from someone who has not asked a single diligence question is usually politeness, not intent. *"What's your cap?"* asked first, before anything about the business, means they are shopping terms, not backing you.

records.name: Priced seed round (preference shares)
records.one_line: Shares sold now at an agreed valuation, with preferential rights.

mechanics.seniority: equity (senior to ordinary via liquidation preference)
mechanics.conversion: optional (to ordinary, on exit or IPO)

disqualifiers.description: cap table with unmodellable prior instruments
founder equity already below a level that survives further dilution

provider.motivation: Fund-return mathematics. They need outcomes that return the whole fund, which is why "good business" is not sufficient and "could be enormous" is necessary.

poisons: non-dilutive programs that test for independence or ownership caps

variants.delta: ESIC-equivalent early-stage investor concessions materially change investor economics before terms are negotiated; wholesale/sophisticated investor certification governs who may be approached at all
NVCA standard docs; accredited investor definition governs the offer
SEIS/EIS eligibility dominates structure — the tax relief is often worth more to the investor than the terms
Fund and family-office density; different professional-investor tests

sources: Summit transcript 2026-08-27 — Kevin Shen on family office process

knowledge.failure_modes: Opening without a cornerstone and drifting for twelve months — named directly on the panel. Setting a valuation with no basis and defending it badly. Raising into a preference stack that makes the next round unfundable. **Increasing the valuation mid-raise, which kills interest outright** — investors read it as having missed out rather than as good news.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"The lead will come once we have momentum."* Inverted — the cornerstone creates the momentum. Dom would not push the button until a cornerstone was secured, after 30–50 conversations. *"Family offices are patient capital so they'll take their time."* They are patient *after* investing; before, time kills deals.
knowledge.ready_signals: A cornerstone in dialogue. Enough traction that the three investor questions have real answers. Clean corporate records. A use-of-funds that maps to growth or technical de-risking with milestones attached.
knowledge.not_ready_signals: Cannot answer "why now." Cap table needs surgery. Every investor conversation is a first conversation — no rung-3 population.
knowledge.tells: *"Come back when you have a lead investor"* is **a soft no** with a door left open. *"What's your timeline?"* early usually means they are deciding whether to bother, not whether to invest. Silence after a data-room grant is a decision.

records.name: Equity crowdfunding / crowd-sourced funding
records.one_line: Many small retail investors buy shares through a licensed platform.

disqualifiers.description: entity type ineligible under the local regime
inability to produce a compliant offer document
a story that does not survive public scrutiny

provider.motivation: Participation and affinity as much as return. Many are buying belonging.

unlocks: a shareholder base that is also a customer base and a marketing channel
poisons: institutional rounds — a cap table with 800 retail holders is a governance objection before it is a valuation objection
taints: some institutional investors decline on cap-table grounds alone

knowledge.failure_modes: Running it without an existing audience and discovering the platform is distribution, not demand. Underestimating the campaign cost. A public failure that is permanently visible.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"The platform brings the investors."* The platform converts an audience you bring. Campaigns are won in the first 48 hours by pre-committed money.
knowledge.tells: A platform that is enthusiastic before asking about your existing audience is selling you a listing, not a raise.

records.name: Convertible note
records.one_line: A loan that becomes equity on a trigger — and stays a loan if it doesn't.

disqualifiers.description: no plausible path to a qualifying financing before maturity
existing senior debt with restrictive covenants

provider.motivation: Downside protection with upside participation. They get paid either way.

unlocks: bridge runway to a priced round
poisons: the next round if the discount stack is aggressive
triggers: a hard maturity date — a cliff with a repayment obligation behind it

forecloses: the ability to ignore a deadline — maturity is real

variants.delta: The local default for early convertibles; more common than SAFEs
Largely displaced by SAFEs at pre-seed; still standard for bridges

knowledge.failure_modes: **It is debt until it converts, and founders reliably forget this.** Maturity arrives, no qualifying round has happened, and the holder is now a creditor with leverage over a company with no cash. Interest accruing silently and materially increasing conversion dilution. Multiple notes with different triggers that interact unpredictably.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"It's basically a SAFE."* No — a SAFE cannot make you insolvent. A note can. The maturity date is the entire difference and it is the thing that bites.
knowledge.ready_signals: A credible, dated path to a qualifying financing comfortably inside the maturity window.
knowledge.not_ready_signals: Using it as a bridge to nowhere. Setting maturity by convention (18/24 months) rather than by when the next round will realistically close.

records.name: Venture debt
records.one_line: Term debt for VC-backed companies, priced off the equity behind it.

disqualifiers.description: runway shorter than the amortisation schedule
existing security over the same assets

provider.motivation: Yield with equity-like optionality, underwritten against the *equity sponsor's* willingness to fund again — not against your business.

blocks: other secured debt against the same assets
poisons: a down round — the debt does not reprice but everything else does

forecloses: flexibility in a downturn — amortisation does not care about your quarter

knowledge.failure_modes: Taking it as a runway extender when the equity story has already broken — the lender is underwriting your investors' conviction, and if that has gone, so has the facility. Covenant breach in a bad quarter converting a financing into a control event.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"It's non-dilutive."* Warrants are dilution, and the covenants are a governance cost that does not appear on the cap table.
knowledge.tells: Heavy focus on who your existing investors are, and light focus on your product, means they are underwriting the sponsor, not you.

records.name: Invoice finance / receivables discounting
records.one_line: Sell or borrow against money customers already owe you.

mechanics.time_to_close: days once facility exists; 2 – 6 weeks to establish

provider.motivation: Underwriting your *customers'* credit, not yours. You are almost incidental.

unlocks: working capital that scales with revenue automatically
blocks: other security over the same receivables

knowledge.failure_modes: Customer concentration making the facility fragile. Non-recourse assumed when the facility is recourse. Notification to customers damaging the relationship.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"We're pre-profit so we can't borrow."* Irrelevant — this instrument does not look at your profitability. It looks at whether your customers pay.

records.name: Revenue-based financing
records.one_line: Capital repaid as a fixed percentage of revenue until a multiple is hit.

disqualifiers.description: revenue that is lumpy or project-based

provider.motivation: Yield underwritten off observable, verifiable revenue data — often via direct integration to your billing system.

knowledge.misconceptions: *"It's cheap because there's no interest rate."* The multiple divided by the repayment period is an interest rate, and on fast repayment it can be very high.

records.name: R&D tax credit / offset
records.one_line: The state refunds a portion of qualifying research and development spend.

mechanics.time_to_close: annual cycle; advance-funding facilities exist against the expected claim

disqualifiers.description: spend already funded by another program

provider.motivation: Industrial policy. They want the activity to happen domestically.

poisons: double-dipping — spend claimed here may be ineligible elsewhere
competes_with: other programs claiming the same expenditure

variants.delta: Refundable offset for companies under a turnover threshold; registration with the program required within a window after year end; eligible activities defined by a core/supporting distinction
SME and RDEC schemes with different mechanics and rates
Crédit d'Impôt Recherche — among the most generous globally, a genuine domicile consideration in itself
SR&ED — long-established, refundable for small CCPCs
Each operates distinct incentive regimes with different eligibility shapes

sources: general knowledge; rates and thresholds deliberately not stated — they change annually and this record's value is structural

knowledge.failure_modes: Reconstructing records after the fact — the single most common and most fatal. Claiming commercial development as research. Missing the registration window. Being unable to evidence *who* did *what* on *which day*.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"We'll sort the paperwork at year end."* The requirement is **contemporaneous** — records made at the time, not assembled later. This is the one instrument where an entity that has been documenting itself continuously for other reasons holds a structural advantage it never built deliberately.
knowledge.ready_signals: Dated technical records generated as a by-product of how work actually happens: version control history, dated design decisions, experiment logs, session records, an append-only ledger of what was attempted and what was learned.
knowledge.not_ready_signals: Technical history that exists only in people's heads or in a chat tool with no export.

records.name: Competitive grant
records.one_line: A funding body selects proposals against published criteria and pays out against milestones.

mechanics.repayable: no (usually; clawback on non-performance is common)
mechanics.time_to_close: 3 – 18 months from open to first payment

disqualifiers.description: activity already commenced where the program requires it not have

provider.motivation: Policy outcomes. **They are buying a result they have been mandated to produce**, and your project is a means to it.

poisons: some programs restrict subsequent commercial arrangements or IP ownership

forecloses: flexibility to pivot the funded work — you are contracted to a scope

knowledge.failure_modes: Writing the application about your company rather than about the program's stated objective. Missing matched-funding requirements. Winning a grant that contracts you to eighteen months of work you no longer want to do. Underestimating acquittal burden.
knowledge.misconceptions: *"It's free money."* It is a contract with milestones, reporting and clawback. And *"the best project wins."* The best *fit to the published criteria* wins — which is a document-comprehension exercise as much as a merit one.
knowledge.tells: A program officer who redirects you to a different program is doing you a significant favour and should be taken literally.

records.name: Government or enterprise procurement as capital
records.one_line: A contract to buy the thing funds building the thing.

disqualifiers.description: cannot meet procurement compliance bar — insurance

provider.motivation: They have a problem and a budget. **Unlike an investor they are not buying upside — they are buying a solved problem.**

unlocks: credibility that no investor can confer

knowledge.misconceptions: *"Government procurement is too slow for a startup."* Often true for open tenders; frequently untrue for pilots, innovation programs, unsolicited proposals and panel arrangements.

records.name: Customer prepayment / annual prepay
records.one_line: The customer pays ahead, in exchange for a discount or terms.

provider.motivation: Discount, priority, influence over roadmap, supply security.

knowledge.misconceptions: *"That's just sales, not funding."* The distinction is accounting, not economics. Twelve months of prepaid revenue and twelve months of runway from a SAFE are the same runway, and one of them costs no equity.

records.name: Paid proof of concept / design partner fee
records.one_line: A prospect pays to co-develop the thing they want to buy.

provider.motivation: They want the capability and would rather shape it than wait for it.

unlocks: product requirements from a paying source
poisons: exclusivity or IP assignment terms that foreclose the wider market

forecloses: depends entirely on IP and exclusivity terms — this is where the one-way risk hides

knowledge.failure_modes: Accepting IP assignment or category exclusivity to win the first cheque, and discovering later it foreclosed the market. Building a bespoke thing that serves one customer and generalises to none.

records.name: Licensing advance / minimum guarantee
records.one_line: A licensee pays upfront against future royalties.

unlocks: proof of third-party valuation of the IP
poisons: territory or field-of-use exclusivity foreclosing other licensees

records.name: Hyperscaler / vendor credits
records.one_line: Compute, tooling or services granted free, which is runway by another name.

provider.motivation: Acquisition cost. They are buying a future paying workload and architectural lock-in at a fraction of enterprise sales cost.

poisons: architectural neutrality — credits are a lock-in instrument wearing a gift's clothing
triggers: which are the most commonly wasted asset in this family

knowledge.failure_modes: Credits expiring unused. Architecting for the credit and inheriting the cost structure when it ends.

records.name: Vendor market development funds / co-op marketing
records.one_line: A vendor funds your go-to-market because your success sells their product.

provider.motivation: Channel leverage — your pipeline is cheaper than their direct sales.

records.name: Corporate venture capital / strategic investment
records.one_line: A corporate invests, usually with a commercial agreement attached.

disqualifiers.description: direct competitive conflict with a portfolio holding

provider.motivation: **Strategic option, not financial return.** They are buying early sight, a hedge, or a supply relationship. The cheque is the smaller half of the transaction.

poisons: acquisition by their competitors; sometimes other CVCs
taints: and some financial investors who read a strategic on the register as a signalled exit
triggers: information rights that may reach a future competitor

knowledge.tells: A strategic that wants information rights but no board seat and no commercial agreement is buying surveillance cheaply.

records.name: SPV per asset / per project
records.one_line: A separate entity holds one asset and raises against that asset alone.

disqualifiers.description: no governance capacity to run multiple entities

classes: any — the SPV selects its own instrument independently
provider.motivation: Isolated exposure to one asset without underwriting an entire company.

unlocks: investors who would never fund the parent
stacks_with: every instrument — the point of the structure

knowledge.failure_modes: Governance overhead exceeding the benefit. Intercompany arrangements that collapse the separation the structure existed to create. Assets that were never actually separable.

records.name: Royalty financing / revenue interest
records.one_line: Capital now in exchange for a percentage of future revenue, forever or to a cap.

disqualifiers.description: revenue not attributable to the financed asset

provider.motivation: Yield uncorrelated to equity markets, secured on a specific stream.

unlocks: capital without dilution or control transfer
poisons: gross margin permanently — the royalty rides ahead of profit

forecloses: a clean margin structure for any future acquirer

records.name: Tokenised real-world asset / revenue share
records.one_line: An on-chain instrument representing a claim on an off-chain asset or revenue stream.

disqualifiers.description: no credible attestation of the underlying asset

provider.motivation: Yield, liquidity in otherwise illiquid assets, portfolio diversification away from correlated crypto assets.

unlocks: a liquidity profile no traditional instrument offers
poisons: institutional equity — many funds cannot hold or sit alongside
triggers: secondary market price discovery you do not control

forecloses: quiet valuation; a token trades and its price is a public claim about you

records.name: Build-for-equity / services-for-equity
records.one_line: A firm does the work and takes stock instead of cash.

mechanics.cost_of_capital_form: equity, usually at an unfavourable implied valuation

provider.motivation: Portfolio exposure on excess capacity; sometimes genuine belief.

unlocks: capability you cannot afford to hire
poisons: cap table cleanliness; institutional investors dislike service providers on the register

knowledge.failure_modes: Misaligned incentive — they are optimising delivery cost, you are optimising outcome. Equity granted for work of uncertain quality with no performance condition. **The implied valuation is usually terrible and rarely calculated.**

records.name: Deferred salary / founder and team forbearance
records.one_line: People work now and are paid later, or in equity.

provider.motivation: Belief, upside, or lack of alternative.

poisons: morale; and an accrued liability that appears in diligence
triggers: a liability on the balance sheet that a future investor will see

records.name: Litigation finance
records.one_line: A funder pays legal costs for a share of the proceeds.

provider.motivation: Uncorrelated returns on legal merit.

unlocks: pursuing a claim you could not otherwise afford — including IP enforcement that protects the core asset

records.name: Islamic finance structures
records.one_line: Capital structures based on profit-and-loss sharing or asset trade rather than interest.

disqualifiers.description: business activity non-compliant under the applicable standards

provider.motivation: Return within a compliance framework, plus mandate alignment.

unlocks: a capital pool measured in trillions that most founders never consider approaching

records.name: Countertrade / offset / barter
records.one_line: Value exchanged without cash, often mandated by a government as a condition of a large contract.

provider.motivation: Defence and infrastructure offset obligations — a prime that has won a large contract may be *required* to place value in-country and is actively looking for recipients.

unlocks: entry to markets that are otherwise closed

records.name: Residency- or citizenship-linked investment
records.one_line: An investor deploys capital partly to obtain residency rights.

disqualifiers.description: entity or activity outside the qualifying definition

provider.motivation: **The return is partly non-financial.** They are buying optionality on where they and their family can live.
